steps.title: Where to start: work from the inside out
steps.body: A fraction stacked inside fractions like this is called a continued fraction. You cannot start at the top, because the top denominator depends on everything below it. The only piece you can compute right away is the deepest one, $3+\frac13$.

steps.title: Flip, then add 3 again
steps.body: The next level up is $3+\cfrac{1}{10/3}$. Dividing $1$ by a fraction flips it, so $\cfrac{1}{10/3} = \frac{3}{10}$ and this level equals $3+\frac{3}{10} = \frac{33}{10}$. Careful: $\frac{33}{10}$ is only the middle level, not the final value. There is one more layer to go.

your_turn.prompt: Before going on: how many '$3+$' layers does the expression have, and how many have we finished so far?
your_turn.answer: Three layers. We have finished two (the innermost $3+\frac13$ and the middle $3+\frac{3}{10}$), so one is left.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The top level is $3$ plus $1$ divided by $\frac{33}{10}$. Dividing by a fraction flips it, so the whole expression is $$3+\frac{10}{33} = \frac{99}{33}+\frac{10}{33} = \frac{109}{33}.$$ Check: $\frac{10}{33}$ is a bit more than $\frac{3}{10}$ but less than $\frac13$, so the value must lie between $3.3$ and $3\frac13$, and $\frac{109}{33} \approx 3.303$ does. The answer is **(D)** $\frac{109}{33}$.

wrong_choices.C: This is the middle level of the fraction, $3+\frac{3}{10}$. It is easy to stop one layer early. Count the '$3+$' layers: there are three of them (the fourth $3$ is the bottom denominator in $\frac13$). Getting $\frac{33}{10}$ means you have handled only two of them.

verification.verifier_notes: Hole found by adversarial verifier, fixed, and re-verified by a fresh verifier.
